subject.title: [Bug]: opencode-go works via direct infer but fails in embedded agent runtime with session takeover

question: Is the merged OpenCode Go stream-termination work plus the open session-takeover recovery PR enough to resolve this provider-specific embedded runtime report, or should OpenCode Go get separate live Telegram/dashboard validation first?
rationale: Source inspection shows adjacent fixes but no current-main proof of the exact provider/model/channel session lifecycle, and choosing between generic recovery and provider-specific follow-up is an owner-boundary decision.

options.title: Require live provider validation
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers or the recovery PR prove `opencode-go/mimo-v2.5` works in direct inference, first embedded turn, follow-up turn, and tool-call turn.

options.title: Treat the generic recovery as sufficient
options.body: Close this only after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89039 lands and maintainers accept its proof as covering the user-visible failure mode.

options.title: Open a narrow provider follow-up
options.body: If live validation still fails after the generic recovery, track a separate OpenCode Go runtime/session fix rather than expanding unrelated session-lock work.

recommendation.title: Require live provider validation
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers or the recovery PR prove `opencode-go/mimo-v2.5` works in direct inference, first embedded turn, follow-up turn, and tool-call turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and adjacent fixes point to Vincent Koc across both the embedded session-lock and OpenCode Go provider surfaces.
